items.t: adidas stock: SP5DER launch adds a new product catalyst
sum: adidas stock traded at 177.53 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:18 CET on Saturday, November 14, 0.07 percent below the Xetra close of Friday, November 13, at 177.65 euros. The week brought a product launch and a derivatives disclosure into focus for investors.

On November 10, adidas announced a new adidas Originals and SP5DER collection led by two neon versions of the F50 Formotion SP5DER. The range combines football-inspired footwear with adidas running tooling and adds tracksuits, graphic T-shirts, a Cordura backpack and co-branded balaclavas, according to the adidas Newsroom.

The collection pre-launched through KINGSPIDER.CO on November 13. A broader release through the CONFIRMED app, selected retailers and selected adidas stores was scheduled for November 14. Footwear is priced at 200 euros, while apparel and accessories range from 70 euros to 140 euros.

On November 12, adidas published a regulatory disclosure concerning NNS Investments (Cyprus) Limited, described as closely associated with supervisory board member Nassef Sawiris. The filing said 87,000 cash-settled short puts linked to adidas shares expired on November 9 outside a trading venue, at a price of 6.8089 euros per contract and an aggregated amount of 592,374.30 euros, according to the adidas investor disclosure.

The two developments address different parts of the investment case: the SP5DER collaboration supports product and lifestyle positioning, while the filing concerns an individual derivative position rather than operating performance. The next trading sessions will show how investors weigh product momentum against the broader earnings outlook.
German equities remain part of the broader market setting tracked in the Current market reports.

sum: adidas reported record third-quarter results on October 29 and raised its full-year operating-profit outlook, according to the adidas Group. The sportswear company said revenue rose 9 percent year over year to 7.252 billion euros in the July-to-September period, while currency-neutral growth reached 7 percent.

adidas stock traded at 177.78 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:18 CET on Friday, November 13, 0.47 percent above the Xetra close of Thursday, November 12. The comparison points to a modestly firmer start after investors had weighed the strong quarter against product-category and execution risks.

Operating profit increased 37 percent to a quarterly record of 1.008 billion euros. The operating margin improved to 13.9 percent from 11.1 percent a year earlier, while net income from continuing operations rose 48 percent to 711 million euros. Earnings per share from continuing operations reached 4.06 euros, compared with 2.57 euros in the prior-year quarter.

Growth was broad but not uniform. Currency-neutral apparel revenue increased 19 percent, performance revenue rose 14 percent and direct-to-consumer sales grew 17 percent. Greater China, North America, Latin America and Japan/South Korea all posted double-digit growth, while Europe declined 4 percent as conservative wholesale sell-in and a planned SAP migration shifted some deliveries into the fourth quarter.

Footwear revenue was flat overall, although direct-to-consumer footwear grew 6 percent. Chief Executive Bjorn Gulden said lifestyle footwear faced excessive inventory and discounting in the marketplace. Management is prioritizing full-price sales and expects conditions to normalize, but the category remains a key test for the brand's margin and growth ambitions.

adidas maintained its forecast for 2026 currency-neutral revenue growth of 9 percent to 10 percent and lifted its operating-profit target to around 2.5 billion euros from around 2.3 billion euros previously. A refund of around 200 million euros related to United States tariff claims supported the third-quarter gross margin, which rose 2.5 percentage points to 54.3 percent.
The company said underlying profitability and the tariff refund would have pointed to operating profit of around 2.6 billion euros.

sum: adidas reported record third-quarter results on October 29, 2026, and raised its full-year operating-profit outlook. The adidas press release showed broad-based growth, although management also pointed to pressure in lifestyle footwear.

Revenue rose 9 percent year over year to 7,252 million euros in the July-to-September period. Currency-neutral revenue increased 7 percent, while operating profit climbed 37 percent to a quarterly record of 1,008 million euros. The operating margin improved to 13.9 percent from 11.1 percent a year earlier.

Net income from continuing operations increased 48 percent to 711 million euros, producing earnings per share of 4.06 euros compared with 2.57 euros in the prior-year quarter. adidas also reported a 2.5 percentage-point improvement in gross margin to 54.3 percent.

The margin benefited from healthy full-price sales and a favorable channel mix, as well as a refund of around 200 million euros related to US tariff claims. The refund was a material one-time contribution to the quarter and should be considered when assessing the underlying margin trend.

Direct-to-consumer sales grew 17 percent on a currency-neutral basis. E-commerce revenue increased 18 percent and own-retail sales advanced 16 percent, with double-digit like-for-like growth across store formats. Performance revenue rose 14 percent, led by running, training and football, while apparel revenue increased 19 percent.

Regional growth was strongest in Japan and South Korea, Latin America, Greater China, North America and emerging markets. Europe was the exception, with revenue declining 4 percent as adidas kept wholesale sell-in conservative amid high inventory levels and promotional activity.

Footwear revenue was flat in the quarter. adidas said lifestyle footwear remained challenged by excess inventory and discounting, while direct-to-consumer footwear sales still grew 6 percent. That split leaves the product mix and inventory normalization important indicators for investors as the company moves into the final quarter.

'Ohio State has invested quite a bit in him' - Insider shares the latest on how close Tennessee is to flipping 5-star EDGE DJ Jacobs from Ohio State
sum: The Tennessee Volunteers are working hard to flip 2027 five-star EDGE DJ Jacobs from the Ohio State Buckeyes.
Tennessee appears to be the main threat to flip 2027 five-star EDGE DJ Jacobs from Ohio State.
The Georgia native has been committed to the Buckeyes for almost a year, but the Vols have continued to recruit him.
Miami and Georgia are also in the mix for Jacobs, but Tennessee is Ohio State’s top competition in this battle.

“Tennessee’s right there in the thick of it,” said VolQuest’s Austin Price on WNML’s Josh and Swain on Wednesday. “I think this is a very open recruitment. Ohio State has invested quite a bit in him from the jump. They’re trying to hold on to him. They’re swinging big to try to make sure they can hold on to him.

“Tennessee and Miami are trying to flip the script on the Buckeyes. So I don’t think that it’s set in stone one way or the other at this point for anybody. And again, Ohio State is the school that he’s been to the most, and it’s the school that he’s been committed to for a while, but I think he is very much open to the possibility of not playing in Columbus if the mood strikes.”

Tennessee has a couple of things working in their favor in this recruiting battle. For one, Jacobs’ father is extremely close with Vols defensive line coach Rodney Garner (Garner was Jacobs’ father’s position coach at Georgia a couple of decades ago).

Lady Vols Star Avery Mills Shares Positive Update in Her Injury Recovery Process
sum: The Tennessee Lady Vols are off to a great start to the 2026-27 women's basketball season, as they have picked up two early non-conference wins. Their first win was against Duquesne, as Kaylene Smikle stole the show with a near-perfect night from the field and 31 points. This set up some high expectations for their next test, which was against Coppin State on the road. In this game, the big headline was Kennedy Fauntleroy going over 1,000 career points.
While the Lady Vols have shown some firepower across the board, it is no secret that one of their best players and additions from the transfer portal has been absent from the court.

Mills is a guard from Lynchburg, Virginia, who was previously with the Liberty Flames. Mills, through two seasons, has found herself in Liberty history, as she set the three-point percentage record with 43.8% in a single season, while also being No. 11 in three-pointers made with 124 through her two seasons of action.

This set the bar extremely high for her first season with the Lady Vols, which was her junior season at-large; however, the talented guard suffered a torn ACL and meniscus on June 30, 2026. This automatically set the standard for the upcoming season, as it became known that she would be out for an extended period of time, and likely the entire season.
On Sunday, Mills showcased that she was back in the gym shooting jump shots on her Instagram story. She also captioned the story with "Little wins day by day. Thank you lord."

This is a massive step forward, as this is just over four months after the injury actually happened. This means that she is on/ahead of schedule. However, while many believe that this could be a sign of her returning to the court in 2026, it still remains reasonable to believe that she will miss the remainder of the season so that she doesn't rush her rehab and will be back next season at full strength.
This is still something worth monitoring, and definitely something worth celebrating if you are a Tennessee Lady Vols basketball fan.

Adidas Korea, Seoul Hold Night Sports Festival for Renovated Guil Station Facilities
sum: Adidas Korea renovated the sports facilities beneath Guil Station along the Anyangcheon stream as part of "Let's Work Out, Seoul," a corporate social responsibility program it runs with the Seoul Metropolitan Government, and held a public "night sports festival" on the 7th to mark the completion.

A range of sports events took place at the newly refurbished futsal court, basketball court, inline skating rink and running track. The futsal court hosted a futsal clinic for youth teams from the Guro District, while the basketball court staged a 3-on-3 friendly match between Adidas employees and the Guro District Office basketball club, as well as a 3-on-3 challenge for residents and other adults in their 20s and 30s. The running track featured a running program joined by running crews from universities in Seoul.

Attendees included Cha Bum-kun, former head coach of the national soccer team; Gu Bon-gil, former national fencing team member; Lee Hye-jung and Song Hae-na, who appear on the soccer variety show "Kick a Goal"; broadcaster Haha, known as a basketball enthusiast; and actor Lee Jae-yoon.

"Let's Work Out, Seoul" is a social contribution campaign that Adidas Korea and the Seoul Metropolitan Government have run jointly since 2017, aimed at improving community sports facilities so residents can enjoy sports safely and conveniently in daily life, and at expanding opportunities to take part in sports. The facilities beneath Guil Station were first renovated by the two partners in 2019, and the latest work improved their safety and usability about seven years later.

GBL stock faces a key NAV test after adidas outlook upgrade
sum: Groupe Bruxelles Lambert's next net asset value update will put its adidas exposure in focus after the sportswear company raised its 2026 operating profit outlook. GBL is scheduled to publish results for the period ended September 30 on Thursday, November 5, according to its financial calendar.

Adidas reported third-quarter operating profit of 1.008 billion euros on October 29 and raised its 2026 outlook from about 2.3 billion euros to about 2.5 billion euros. The upgrade followed a US customs duty refund of about 200 million euros, according to an Opulion analysis published on October 31.

For GBL investors, the distinction between the reported improvement and underlying operating progress matters. Opulion said GBL held 3.53 percent of adidas's share capital at June 30 and that the stake represented 8.7 percent of GBL's net asset value at that date. The September 30 valuation will therefore provide a new reference point for the portfolio before later adidas developments.

GBL's release is expected to show the portfolio valuation at the end of September, including the market value of its holdings. The timing means the figure will be assessed against subsequent developments in the Recordati transaction and the latest performance of major portfolio companies, rather than treated as a standalone earnings measure.

GBL is a Brussels-based investment holding company with investments in listed and private businesses. Its portfolio approach makes changes in the market value of major holdings central to the net asset value reported to shareholders.
Belgian equities remain the relevant market backdrop for investors following GBL; see current market reports.

Earnings Beat: adidas AG Just Beat Analyst Forecasts, And Analysts Have Been Updating Their Models
sum: Investors in adidas AG (ETR:ADS) had a good week, as its shares rose 7.0% to close at €169 following the release of its quarterly results. It looks like a credible result overall - although revenues of €7.3b were what the analysts expected, adidas surprised by delivering a (statutory) profit of €4.08 per share, an impressive 21% above what was forecast. Earnings are an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance, look at what the analysts are forecasting for next year, and see if there's been a change in sentiment towards the company. We've gathered the most recent statutory forecasts to see whether the analysts have changed their earnings models, following these results.

Taking into account the latest results, the consensus forecast from adidas' 28 analysts is for revenues of €29.2b in 2027. This reflects a meaningful 9.6% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are predicted to surge 26% to €11.76. Before this earnings report, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of €29.0b and earnings per share (EPS) of €11.64 in 2027. The consensus analysts don't seem to have seen anything in these results that would have changed their view on the business, given there's been no major change to their estimates.

The analysts reconfirmed their price target of €200, showing that the business is executing well and in line with expectations. It could also be instructive to look at the range of analyst estimates, to evaluate how different the outlier opinions are from the mean. The most optimistic adidas analyst has a price target of €245 per share, while the most pessimistic values it at €160. As you can see, analysts are not all in agreement on the stock's future, but the range of estimates is still reasonably narrow, which could suggest that the outcome is not totally unpredictable.

Of course, another way to look at these forecasts is to place them into context against the industry itself. The analysts are definitely expecting adidas' growth to accelerate, with the forecast 7.6% annualised growth to the end of 2027 ranking favourably alongside historical growth of 4.2% per annum over the past five years.

sum: Investing.com -- Adidas AG (ETR:ADSGn) on Thursday reported record third-quarter results, with operating profit reaching an all-time high of €1 billion, prompting the company to lift its full-year profit outlook to around €2.5 billion from a previous target of around €2.3 billion.
The sportswear giant's shares rose 3.6% in German trading by 10:17 GMT.

Adidas posted revenue of €7.3 billion for the quarter, up 9% from the prior year and 7% on a currency-neutral basis, exceeding the analyst consensus of €7.2 billion. Operating profit surged 37% to €1.0 billion, representing a margin of 13.9%, up 2.8 percentage points YoY.

The company's gross margin improved 2.5 percentage points to 54.3%, reflecting a tariff refund of around €200 million as well as healthy full-price sales. Net income from continuing operations increased 48% to €711 million, or €4.06 per share.

Revenue growth was led by apparel, which increased 19% on a currency-neutral basis, driven by strong demand across Performance and Lifestyle categories. Footwear revenues remained flat as the company maintained a conservative wholesale approach amid a promotional marketplace, though direct-to-consumer footwear sales grew 6%. DTC sales overall jumped 17%, with e-commerce up 18% and own retail up 16%.

Geographically, currency-neutral sales grew double-digits in Greater China (+13%), North America (+12%), Latin America (+16%), and Japan/South Korea (+19%). Europe declined 4%, impacted by the company's conservative wholesale sell-in approach and a temporary impact from an SAP ERP migration at the end of the quarter.

"We achieved the highest revenue ever in a quarter with €7,252 million and the highest operating profit ever with €1,008 million," said CEO Bjørn Gulden. "Our brand, our product and our people are our strength."

items.t: NIKE vs. adidas: Which Stock Offers Stronger Growth Potential?
sum: The global sportswear industry is witnessing an intensifying battle for market dominance as industry heavyweights NIKE, Inc. NKE and adidas AG ADDYY compete for consumer loyalty, innovation leadership and market share. NIKE remains the world's leading athletic footwear and apparel company, while Germany-based adidas stands as its formidable challenger, leveraging its sporting heritage, product innovation and strong lifestyle appeal.

Both companies design, market and distribute athletic footwear, apparel and accessories through wholesale networks, company-operated stores and digital platforms. While NIKE is focused on revitalizing its brand momentum and defending its market leadership, adidas is capitalizing on evolving consumer preferences and lifestyle trends. Against this backdrop, which sportswear giant offers stronger investment potential? Let us find out.

NIKE maintains a dominant position in the global sporting goods industry, supported by a diversified portfolio of footwear, apparel and accessories. Its Performance business generated $16 billion in fiscal 2026 revenues and grew in the high single digits in first-quarter fiscal 2027. Running delivered double-digit growth, while NIKE nearly tripled its share of the Max cushioning category in the past year, reinforcing its competitive strength.

NIKE's Sport Offense strategy emphasizes innovation, sport-specific assortments and stronger consumer engagement. Its portfolio spans Running, Basketball, Football, Training and Sportswear, targeting athletes and lifestyle-conscious consumers. Women's Basketball signature revenues expanded nearly 500% between fiscal 2022 and 2026. Meanwhile, NIKE is strengthening digital distribution in China, restoring Jordan Brand exclusivity and leveraging product innovations to reinforce its premium positioning.

However, financial headwinds persist. First-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues declined 4% to $11.2 billion, reflecting weakness in Sportswear, Jordan Brand and Greater China. Nevertheless, the gross margin improved 60 basis points to 42.8%, while earnings reached 48 cents per share. Its Pace transformation initiative targets $2.5 billion in savings, potentially supporting operational efficiency and long-term profitability despite near-term revenue pressures.

Adidas Stock Plunges 12% Despite World Cup Revenue Boost
sum: Adidas dominated the World Cup as the sponsor of the final two teams, Spain and Argentina, the match-day ball, and even the referees. The quadrennial event pushed revenue to a quarterly record of €6.7 billion ($7.7 billion based on current exchange rates), and the German sports giant raised its year-end revenue forecast.
“Being the CEO of Adidas is a privilege,” Adidas boss Bjørn Gulden said when announcing the company’s second-quarter results on Thursday. “Being the CEO of Adidas during a World Cup is even better.”

Yet the market severely punished Adidas’ stock, sending shares down 12% at the close in Germany, the third biggest one-day fall since it went public in 1995. The problem was on the expense side, which came in more than $200 million ahead of expectations. Marketing expenses rose $243 million, with campaigns tied to the FIFA event, resulting in operating income of €574 million ($660 million), versus expectations of $770 million.

“Strong Q2 growth momentum underpinned an impressive gross profit beat,” wrote Jefferies analyst James Grzinic in a post-earnings research note. “Unhelpfully for the shares today, this was more than paired back by a remarkable hike in [operating expenses].”
Adidas’ revenue rose 13% for the quarter—it was 14% currency neutral. Annual revenue is expected to grow between 9% and 10%, up from prior guidance of high-single digits.

The performance business surged 39%, fueled by strong growth in soccer, running and training footwear. Gulden said it compensated for a “weaker and more difficult lifestyle footwear market.” Lifestyle faced pressure from heavy discounting at many retailers, especially in Europe. Overall footwear revenue of €3.5 billion ($4.2 billion) was flat.

Apparel revenue surged 34% to €2.7 billion ($3.1 billion). The company said double-digit growth in soccer and Original apparel was complemented by “strong increases” in running training, motorsport and U.S. sports.

NIKE's Turnaround Story: Are Earnings Finally Finding Footing?
sum: After several quarters of sales pressure and margin headwinds, investors are closely watching whether NIKE Inc. NKE is beginning to establish a more durable earnings recovery. The company has embarked on a broad turnaround effort centered on its "Win Now" strategy, which aims to restore marketplace health, strengthen product innovation and improve execution across both wholesale and direct channels. While the recovery remains a work in progress, management has pointed to improving trends in key performance categories as evidence that the foundation is strengthening.

A key component of the turnaround is NIKE's effort to reset its portfolio and distribution model. The company has been reducing excess inventory, repositioning classic franchises and concentrating resources on innovation-led growth areas such as running, basketball and global football. At the same time, NIKE is rebuilding relationships with wholesale partners to improve product visibility and consumer reach. These actions are intended to enhance sell-through rates, support healthier pricing dynamics and gradually improve the quality of revenue generation.

Earnings recovery, however, is still facing meaningful challenges. Higher tariffs, promotional activity and costs associated with marketplace restructuring continue to pressure profitability, while demand trends remain uneven across regions. Nevertheless, improving inventory discipline and stronger performance in strategic categories suggest that the business is moving in the right direction. If NIKE can successfully execute its turnaround initiatives while restoring a greater mix of full-price sales, earnings may finally find a firmer footing after a prolonged period of transition.
adidas AG ADDYY and lululemon athletica inc. LULU are NKE's key competitors in the global market.

The company has benefited from robust demand in football, running and Originals, while a better product mix and higher full-price sell-through have supported margin expansion. items.t: Adidas vs. Puma: The Family Rift That Shaped the Sportswear Industry
sum: A bitter family feud gave rise to two of the world’s most famous footwear brands.
A rift between two Bavarian brothers, Adolf “Adi” Dassler and Rudolf “Rudi” Dassler, created two of the world’s most iconic footwear companies.

But before this legendary family feud fueled the Adidas and Puma rivalry, before they competed in arenas and before they built factories on opposite sides of their hometown river, the brothers worked together to transform the sneaker industry.
King Henry VIII of England wore the first pair of soccer boots, but the footwear didn’t take off until several centuries later.

When Adi and his older brother Rudi returned from fighting in World War I, they started making and selling shoes out of their mother’s house in Herzogenaurach, a sleepy town in Bavaria, Germany. In 1924, they officially formed the Gebrüder Dassler Schuhfabrik, the Dassler Brothers Sports Shoe Factory.

In the 1920s, the athletic shoe market was much smaller than it is today. People weren’t wearing athletic shoes for casual errands or as a fashion statement. Yet both brothers saw a future in sports footwear, and they had developed their own specialties within the field.

“Adi is more of a shoemaker, Rudi more of a salesperson,” says Nick Smith, author of Kicks: The Great American Story of Sneakers and host of Sneakernomics, a BBC podcast. “You were dealing with equal players here.”

What Does the Debut of the Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3 Spell for adidas?
sum: If adidas marketeers sat in a room and tried to devise the best possible debut for the Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3, the success of the London Marathon would have been a moon shot. Nevertheless, last Sunday three marathoners broke records and displayed feats of superhuman ability – all wearing the brand-spanking-new supershoe.

The London event was the first time the Pro Evo 3 was worn in a competitive race, and saw Kenya’s Sabastian Sawe and Ethiopia’s Yomif Kejelcha run in under two hours, setting times of 1:59:30 and 1:59:41, respectively – firsts of their kind. In the women’s race, Ethiopian athlete Tigst Assefa set a new record, completing the 42km distance in 2:15:41.

adidas have revelled in the success, and they deserve it – because the Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3 represents the kind of technological jump paramount to winning the race of reaching the perfect supershoe.

The successes of the Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3 don’t come as a total surprise, with the franchise last year sitting on more podiums at Marathon Majors than any other brand. As a group, the line has helped break three world records and win over 30 key road races.

What these stats tells us is that the Trefoil lab in Herzogenaurach are doing something right when it comes to innovation. Disregard the victories from Sunday, and the Pro Evo 3 is still the lightest elite race-day shoe from the brand, weighing in at approximately 97 grams – 30 per cent less than the Pro Evo 2! It’s also said to improve forefoot energy return by 11 per cent and increase running economy by 1.6 per cent when compared to its predecessor.

‘The adidas family is incredibly proud of Sabastian and Tigst’s historic achievements,’ said Patrick Nava, General Manager at adidas Running. ‘[This] marks the fastest times humans have ever run in a marathon. This is a testament to the years of hard work and dedication they have made, alongside our innovation team, who have built a supershoe which breaks new ground in the Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3.’

Following this triumph, adidas shares rose almost 2 per cent on Monday and the $500 limited release of the Pro Evo 3 sold out within minutes (partially expected, as elite race-day shoes regularly sell through upon first launch).

Are U.S. Tariffs a Structural Headwind for lululemon's Margins?
sum: lululemon athletica inc.LULU is facing U.S. tariffs as a structural headwind to its margins, although the impact can be partly managed through strategies and cost-control execution. Tariffs have become a significant cost pressure for the company. Such costs are expected to persist, making them a structural element within the company’s cost base. Consequently, these are adding up to extra costs, and weighing on gross margins and overall profitability.

During fourth-quarter fiscal 2025 results, although revenues and earnings per share (EPS) beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate, the bottom line fell year over year, reflecting margin pressure from higher markdowns, tariff-related costs and elevated selling, general and administrative expenses.

The gross profit dipped 8% year over year while the gross margin contracted 550 basis points (bps) in the same quarter, primarily affected by a 560-bps decline in the product margin, led by increased markdowns and tariff impacts. Tariffs had a gross negative impact of 520 bps in the quarter, partly offset by 110 bps from enterprise efficiency initiatives. Notably, markdowns increased 130 bps and fixed-cost deleverage weighed by 30 bps.

In fiscal 2025, the company incurred gross tariff expenses of $275 million. Through targeted mitigation strategies, including sourcing adjustments and cost efficiencies, the company offset $62 million of this burden, outperforming the initial expectations. Tariff pressures are expected to intensify, with gross costs projected to reach $380 million in fiscal 2026. To counter this, the company plans to leverage its enterprise-wide efficiency initiatives, which are anticipated to generate $160 million in offsets within the gross margin, helping cushion the overall impact.

The company has been working to mitigate the impact. Efforts such as improving full-price sales, reducing markdowns, optimizing inventory and diversifying its supply chain are helping to somewhat offset the tariff burden. While tariff costs cannot be fully avoided, effective execution and strategic adjustments can help partially contain their impact.

Bank of America downgrades Adidas and JD Sports, shares tumble
sum: Adidas and JD Sports tumbled on Tuesday after Bank of America downgraded its stance on the sportswear retailers, saying it expects a "material stepdown" in the sector’s growth.
The bank cut Adidas to ‘underperform’ from ‘buy’ and slashed the price target to €160 from €213. JD Sports was downgraded to ‘neutral’ from ‘buy’ and the price target cut to 96p from 112p.
Analysts at the bank said the 20-year "casualisation trend" was largely complete.

As far as Adidas is concerned, BoA said the sports performance segment offers no relief as sport participation, in the US at least, is not increasing. It also pointed to the fact that Nike and Adidas are not expanding their retail exposure as a share of revenue and said this removes the technical boost of moving sales from wholesale to retail.

Bank of America said JD Sports' cost structure is largely fixed so revenue weakness creates a margin risk. It also noted that the third-quarter trading statement indicated no pre-tax profit rise in FY27. This points to further consensus earnings per share downgrades, it said.
At 1110 GMT, JD Sports shares were down 5.5% at 82.63p, while Adidas was 7% weaker at €158.05.

Hey Dude Taps Former Adidas Exec Rupert Campbell as President
sum: Rupert Campbell, the brand’s senior vice president and chief commercial officer, has been promoted to executive vice president and brand president of Hey Dude, effective immediately. He will report to Crocs Inc. CEO Andrew Rees.
Campbell joined the company in March 2025. In his new role, he will have oversight for leading the brand’s product, marketing and commercial go-to market strategy.

“Rupert has proven to be an instrumental part of the Hey Dude leadership team, driving global strategy and execution end-to-end across all parts of our Hey Dude business,” Rees said. He added that Crocs’ board and leadership team are “confident that he will guide the Hey Dude business to long-term scalable global growth.”
“I’m honored for the opportunity to expand my role within the Hey Dude brand and ignite the next phase of our journey, Campbell said.

Prior to joining Crocs, Campbell was a 9-year veteran of Adidas North America where he most recently served as president. In that role, he led a market of more than $6 billion in revenue and a team of more than 10,000. During his tenure at Adidas, he also held various leadership positions across several international regions, including Europe and Russia, working on transforming consumer perception of the brand and building marketshare.

In the third quarter , Rees said quarterly results came in ahead of expectations for the Hey Dude brand. The CEO also said that the brand returned to the Top 10 list of preferred brands among males in the latest Piper Sandler survey this fall.
Hey Dude earlier this month launched its NHL Collection for hockey fans featuring its cozy Wally Slipper. The slipper has a slip-on silhouette with faux shearling.
